title: Tipos y categorías de controles
description: A control has one category (how it is implemented) and one or more types (what it achieves). Questions often ask for one dimension only.
rows: Technical
Category
Implemented by systems through hardware, software, or firmware (CompTIA's term; other frameworks say logical).
Firewall rules, encryption, MFA, EDR, OS permissions
Managerial
Category
Administrative controls focused on governing and managing risk and the security program.
Policies, risk assessments, security planning, vendor reviews
Operational
Category
Carried out day to day by people rather than by systems.
Security awareness training, configuration management, log review procedures, incident handling by staff
Physical
Category
Tangible measures that protect facilities, equipment, and people.
Fences, bollards, door locks, badge readers, mantraps (access control vestibules)
Preventive
Type
Stops an incident from happening in the first place.
Firewall deny rule, door lock, account lockout, least privilege
Deterrent
Type
Discourages an attacker psychologically without physically stopping them.
Warning signs, login banners, visible cameras, bright lighting
Detective
Type
Identifies and records an incident while or after it happens.
IDS, SIEM alerts, log review, motion sensors, recorded video
Corrective
Type
Reduces impact and restores normal operation after an incident.
Restoring from backup, reimaging a host, patching an exploited flaw, IR playbook
Compensating
Type
Alternative control used when the primary control is not feasible, providing similar protection.
Isolating an unpatchable legacy system on its own VLAN; extra monitoring when separation of duties is impossible
Directive
Type
Tells people what they must or must not do; relies on compliance rather than enforcement.
Policies, AUP, procedures, "Authorized personnel only" signs
Exam tip
Both
Answer the dimension asked: a firewall is technical (category) and preventive (type). Deterrent discourages; directive instructs.
A camera is a physical control whose type is detective (recording) and deterrent (when visible).
